blocks.text: One way to read Proverbs 8 is within the larger pattern of Proverbs 1–9, where Wisdom and Folly are portrayed as women whose public calls, houses, meals, and paths embody rival desires leading toward life or death. Here Wisdom speaks in public places, calls people to receive instruction, and presents her way as righteousness and justice. In verses 22–31, this speaking Wisdom describes her relation to YHWH’s ordering of the world, rejoicing before him and delighting in humanity. This portrayal gives the chapter’s invitation unusual breadth: Wisdom is not presented merely as useful advice, but as bound to the order of the world itself.
